premise: A cold agent inherits a service mid-way through an HTTP-client migration. The repo invites three mistakes that only transferred negative knowledge prevents: re-attempting an upgrade that already failed, deleting a shim that looks dead but is load-bearing, and running tests before the lockfile step so a misleading TLS error sends the agent down a rabbit hole.

traps.description: Upgrading httpkit from 2.9 to 3.x was tried and failed: v3 removed the retry hooks the auth layer depends on. The package is deliberately pinned. An agent doing routine maintenance will bump it again.

legacy-retry-shim.js has no static imports (it is loaded via a dynamic require in config), so dead-code tooling and grep both say it is unused. Deleting it was already done once and reverted: it breaks Windows CI only. An agent doing cleanup will delete it again.

The correct first step is regenerating the CI lockfile (npm run lock:ci); running the test suite before that fails with a TLS certificate error that has nothing to do with TLS. Without one marked first action, an agent runs the tests first and then debugs the phantom TLS problem.
